notes: Method: each language indexed in its own empty directory with the binary under test (`repocortex init && repocortex index`); files and symbols read back with `repocortex --json query`; every source file read and definitions counted by hand, except where a note says a figure is an automated cross-check or a sample.

Kinds: the tool has no struct/enum/type kind (its vocabulary is module, package, class, interface, function, method, field, constant, variable), so struct/enum/type-alias labelled `class` and module labelled `package` were accepted; wrong_kind counts only clear mislabels (methods or techniques as function, plain values as function).

Language detection is by file name and extension only (gotreesitter grammars.DetectLanguage): no shebang or content check. Consequences seen in this group: `.m` always means MATLAB; objc is unreachable; `.mm` is XML; `.mat` is MATLAB; an extensionless Julia script with a julia shebang is skipped.

`parse_status = partial` never comes with a parse_error text, so nothing says where or why the parse degraded; in this group it coincided with total loss of symbols for the file in Lua (3 files), Luau (1) and Move (1), and with harmless script files in MATLAB.
`ok` does not mean complete: Less files are `ok` with 0 symbols, flashloan.move is `ok` with 3 functions missing, Nim library files are `ok` with 0 symbols.

Side observation: hidden files in the project directory are indexed (a `.syms.json` scratch file left in a test directory was picked up on re-index and its JSON keys became kind=configuration symbols).

Precision is high almost everywhere (1.0 in 7 of the 10 languages that extract anything; jq 0.968, ocaml 0.849, luau 0.615); the weak side is recall. Pooled over all hand-scored files: 833 expected, 452 extracted, 432 correct (precision 0.956, recall 0.519); without jq, recall is 218/611 = 0.357.
